correction_to_earlier_framing.consequence: The correct external comparison for our arms is GCBC 1 ±1 and the other -play-v0 baselines, all <=4. Under that comparison our result is a faithful reproduction. The MVP/FMQ numbers must be dropped from any comparison table, not merely labeled with a different paradigm.
correction_to_earlier_framing.error: Earlier notes in this repository compared our -play-v0 goal-conditioned results against MVP (0.32-0.52) and FMQ+QGBS (0.88) on cube-triple. Those numbers are from cube-triple-play-SINGLETASK-task4-v0.
correction_to_earlier_framing.why_it_was_wrong: Per the official OGBench repository, singletask variants are for standard reward-maximizing offline RL, while -play-v0 is goal-conditioned. The documentation states the two settings 'target fundamentally different problem formulations, so direct success rate comparisons would not be meaningful.'

purpose: Determine whether the uniform zero on cube-triple reflects a defect in our pipeline or reproduces known benchmark behavior.

verdict.reasoning: Published GCBC -- the direct BC-class analogue of our arms -- scores 1 ±1 on cube-triple-play-v0, statistically indistinguishable from our 0/60 whose 95% upper bound is 4.87%. EVERY method in the original paper scores <=4 on this task, including value-based ones. Our zero reproduces known benchmark behavior rather than revealing a defect.
verdict.task_is_near_zero_for_everyone: cube-triple-play is the hardest cube task by a wide margin: GCIQL falls 68 -> 40 -> 3 from single to double to triple. It is effectively unsolved in the goal-conditioned setting, not merely hard for BC.
